title.rendered: Rooted, Built Up, Abounding in Thanksgiving: Growing Deep in Christ | The Thankful Heart, Day 7

excerpt.rendered: Colossians 2:6-7 pictures believers rooted and built up in Christ, abounding with thanksgiving. Day 7 of The Thankful Heart goes deep in Him.

content.rendered:
A tree does not strain to bear fruit. It sinks its roots deep and the fruit comes. Paul says a life rooted in Christ does the same, and the fruit it bears most is thanksgiving.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, November 21, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 7

Today’s Scripture

“As you therefore have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him, rooted and built up in Him and established in the faith, as you have been taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving.”
Colossians 2:6-7 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

We are halfway through The Thankful Heart, and Paul gives us a picture of where all this gratitude grows from. It starts with a simple sentence: “As you therefore have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him.” How did you receive Christ? Not by effort, not by merit, but by grace through faith. Paul says, keep walking the same way. The Christian life does not begin in grace and then switch to hard work. It continues as it began: receiving.

Then Paul piles up pictures. Rooted is a farming word. Built up is a building word. Established is a legal word, meaning confirmed or made firm. Roots go down into Christ and draw life from Him. The building rises on Him as the foundation. The faith is settled and secure because He is faithful. Notice that every one of these words is in Him. Your stability is not in your feelings, your track record or your circumstances. It is in Christ.

And what grows from roots like these? “Abounding in it with thanksgiving.” Abounding means overflowing, running over the sides. Thanksgiving is not the root; it is the fruit. You do not become rooted by trying harder to be grateful. You become grateful because you are rooted. When your life is drawing from Christ, gratitude rises naturally, like sap in a healthy tree.

This matters, because seasons change. The tree in a Nairobi garden faces dry months as well as rainy ones. What keeps it alive is not the weather but the roots. Some of you are in a dry season right now. The good news is that your roots are not in the season. They are in Him, and He does not change. Jeremiah describes the one who trusts in the Lord as a tree planted by the waters that does not fear when heat comes (Jeremiah 17:7-8).

So take a moment today to go back to the root. Remind yourself how you received Christ: freely, as a gift. Thank Him that you are in Him, rooted, built up and established. Then watch what happens. Thanksgiving starts to overflow, not because you forced it, but because you remembered where you are planted.

How the Thankful Heart Grows

It keeps walking the way it began. We received Christ by grace, and we walk in Him by grace.

It is rooted in Christ, not in circumstances. Seasons change; the roots stay in Him.

It overflows instead of straining. Thanksgiving is the fruit of deep roots, not the work that grows them.

Declaration

Lord Jesus, I thank You that I have received You as my Lord, and I walk in You the same way, by grace (Colossians 2:6). I thank You that I am rooted and built up in You and established in the faith. I thank You that I am like a tree planted by the waters, and I do not fear when the heat comes (Jeremiah 17:7-8). My life draws from You, and my heart abounds with thanksgiving. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
